In LaTeX, you can align the caption of a table to the left without using the `caption` package by redefining the `\@makecaption` command or by using the `tabular` environment with manual formatting. Here are two approaches:

### **Method 1: Redefine `\@makecaption` (for all tables)**
Add this to your preamble (before `\begin{document}`):

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    \parbox[t]{\hsize}{\caption@font\caption@style{#1: }#2\par}
  \else
    \global \@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{\hfil\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

This modifies the default caption behavior to left-align captions.

### **Method 2: Manually Format the Caption (for a single table)**
If you only need to left-align a single table caption, you can use:

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
    \hline
    A & B & C \\
    \hline
    1 & 2 & 3 \\
    \hline
  \end{tabular}
  \caption*{\raggedright Your left-aligned caption here} % Use \caption* to avoid numbering
\end{table}
```

Or, if you want to keep the caption number but left-align it:

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
    \hline
    A & B & C \\
    \hline
    1 & 2 & 3 \\
    \hline
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{\raggedright Your left-aligned caption here}
\end{table}
```

### **Method 3: Use `\captionof` from `caption` (if you can use a package)**
If you can use the `caption` package, the simplest way is:

```latex
\usepackage{caption}
\captionsetup{justification=raggedright}
```

But since you asked for a solution **without** the `caption` package, **Method 1** (redefining `\@makecaption`) is the most general solution.

Would you like a solution for a specific document class (e.g., `report`, `article`, `book`)? Let me know!
